s: A retail company needs to provide a series of data files to another company, which is its business partner. These files are saved in an Amazon S3 bucket under Account A, which belongs to the retail company. The business partner company wants one of its IAM users, User_DataProcessor, to access the files from its own AWS account (Account B). Which combination of steps must the companies take so that User_DataProcessor can access the S3 bucket successfully? (Select TWO.)
o: Turn on the cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) feature for the S3 bucket in Account A.

w.y: Cross-account S3 access needs two grants. The bucket policy in Account A must allow Account B's user or account, and Account B must give User_DataProcessor an IAM identity policy that allows the S3 actions on that bucket. CORS applies only to browsers making cross-origin requests and does not grant any permissions. The correct bucket policy (C) names Principal arn:aws:iam::<Account B>:user/User_DataProcessor and allows s3:GetObject (and s3:ListBucket) on the bucket and bucket/* ARNs; the correct IAM policy (D) allows the same actions on the same resources.

o.A: CORS controls browser cross-origin requests and grants no IAM or bucket permissions to another account.
o.B: Policy text missing (it was an image in the source PDF), so this option can't be judged.
o.C: Policy text missing; the key says this is the bucket policy in Account A that grants Account B's user access.
o.D: Policy text missing; the key says this is the identity policy in Account B that allows User_DataProcessor to use the bucket.
o.E: Policy text missing (it was an image in the source PDF), so this option can't be judged.

s: How can I provide cross-account access to objects in S3 buckets?

nt: The four policies (B–E) were images in the PDF and are missing here, so B vs C and D vs E can't be told apart from the text. Answer from the principle instead: which two grants does cross-account S3 access need? The Why section describes what the correct policies contain.
